name: Lords Supper
overview: The Lord's Supper is a sacred ordinance instituted by Jesus Christ during the Last Supper, where He took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to His disciples as His body given for them, commanding them to do this in remembrance of Him. This act, recorded in Matthew, Mark, and Luke, symbolizes Christ's sacrificial death and the new covenant between God and believers. The early church faithfully continued this practice, gathering on the first day of the week to break bread together, as seen in Acts, emphasizing fellowship, apostolic teaching, and prayer. The Lord's Supper points forward to the future fulfillment when Christ will drink anew with His followers in the Father's kingdom.
